openings.claim: Stratifying counters by deployment interval might separate load-associated and release-associated explanations.
openings.discriminator: Compare persistence at similar load across releases versus within-release persistence across load bands. Release effects predict shifts at comparable load; load effects predict similar load relationships across releases. Neither pattern would defeat this discriminator’s usefulness.
openings.probe: Proposed only: inspect existing aggregate strata; document missing or confounded comparisons before assigning a cause.
openings.uncertainty: Counters may conceal request mix; no causal attribution is established.

openings.claim: Aligning queue events and latency spikes could distinguish queue buildup from a downstream stall.
openings.discriminator: Queue-first and downstream-first accounts predict different temporal orderings. Reliable opposite ordering defeats each respective account; unresolved clock error defeats the ordering test itself.
openings.probe: Proposed only: first determine whether synchronized timestamps exist, then bound timing error and inspect ordering.
openings.uncertainty: Synchronized timestamps are indispensable; existence is unknown. No permission change is assumed.

Retains temporal alternatives, respective defeat conditions, clock-error failure, indispensable resource and declared uncertain fit.

Declared violates: injecting downstream delay might reproduce a signature; controlled delay predicts stall-like ordering. Failure to reproduce weakens but does not eliminate the stall account. Injection changes service, breaching read-only investigation; probe remains parked and unauthorized. Signature resemblance and perturbation transfer are untested.

decision: Retain D1 and resource-dependent D2 for auditable narrowing only. All proposals are synthetic and untested; no real observations or live access exist. Counters are hypothetical. Investigation stays read-only, raw customer payloads remain within the service boundary, and every causal conclusion must identify a falsifiable alternative. Unknown resources grant no constraint relaxation.
